item.title: Presbyterian church weighing options on 300 Bloor St. West office agreement
item.description: The Presbyterian Church in Canada (PCC) has announced it is re-evaluating its course of action on a plan to share office space with the United Church of Canada following the Anglican Church of Canada’s withdrawal from that plan. “The PCC understands that important factors in the originally proposed ecumenical project have changed significantly,” reads a Dec. 12 press release. The post Presbyterian church weighing options on 300 Bloor St. West office agreement appeared first on Anglican Journal.

item.title: Primate criticizes hate speech law amendment
item.description: Archbishop Shane Parker, primate of the Anglican Church of Canada, has written an open letter asking the Canadian government to reconsider an amendment to an upcoming bill that would remove religion as a defence against hate speech charges— while other critics describe the bill itself as an attack on free speech. The post Primate criticizes hate speech law amendment appeared first on Anglican Journal.

item.description: The Atlantic School of Theology (AST) will establish a pioneering ecumenical shared ministries training program after receiving a US$2.5-million grant from the Lilly Endowment foundation. item.title: Meet General Synod’s new chancellor, George Cadman
item.description: Cadman, who spoke with the Anglican Journal in January, became the national church’s chancellor—a volunteer officer of General Synod who provides advice on both secular and church law—on Jan. 1. The post Meet General Synod’s new chancellor, George Cadman appeared first on Anglican Journal.

item.title: Mixed-ecology church model growing in Anglican parishes
item.description: The Church of England declared in its vision and strategy for the 2020s that one of its three priorities was to “be a church where mixed ecology is the norm”. But the concept of a “mixed-ecology” church, in which a traditional parish co-exists with new expressions of church, has also become increasingly popular within the Anglican Church of Canada. item.title: Cult of King Charles the Martyr reflects enduring political divisions
item.description: A cult of martyrdom began forming around Charles Stuart—who, as reigning monarch of England, Scotland and Ireland, was known as King Charles I—almost immediately after his execution for high treason on Jan. 30, 1649. item.title: Pushing forward on the trail of spiritual discipline
item.description: I recently went to a Habitat for Humanity ReStore on Belfast Road in Ottawa to donate some items (and to check out the used tools). The store is in an industrial building which used to house the automotive machine shop I worked in for the better part of two years in the late 1970s. item.title: May the drumbeat of your heart be a celebration of life
item.description: FEATHER: Creator God, we give you thanks for this new day and all days. We ask that you forgive our failures to heed your word and call, grant us your spirit of peace and guide us to walk in humility and with an open heart.
